name: Eastern Wei
summary: The eastern half of the Northern Wei after the court split in 534, ruled from Ye by the general Gao Huan behind a puppet emperor.

fell.text: Gao Yang deposed the last Eastern Wei emperor in 550 and founded the Northern Qi.

name: Western Wei
summary: The western half of the Northern Wei, ruled from Chang'an by Yuwen Tai, whose family replaced it with the Northern Zhou; its garrison militia became the model for the Sui and Tang armies.

fell.text: Yuwen Jue took the throne from the last Western Wei emperor in 557 and founded the Northern Zhou.

name: Northern Qi
summary: The Gao family state that held the richer eastern half of the north, remembered for its Buddhist cave temples at Xiangtangshan and its court chaos.

fell.text: The Northern Zhou took Ye in 577 and reunited the north.

name: Northern Zhou
summary: The Yuwen family state at Chang'an that conquered the Northern Qi in 577 and united the north, four years before its general Yang Jian took the throne as founder of the Sui.

fell.text: Yang Jian took the Northern Zhou throne in 581 and founded the Sui.

name: Later Tang
summary: The second of the Five Dynasties, founded by the Shatuo Turk Li Cunxu, who destroyed the Later Liang in 923 and claimed the Tang name; it also took Sichuan for a decade.

fell.text: Shi Jingtang, with Khitan help, took Luoyang at the start of 937 and founded the Later Jin, ceding the Sixteen Prefectures around Beijing to the Liao.

name: Later Jin
summary: The third of the Five Dynasties, set up by Shi Jingtang as a client of the Khitan Liao, to whom he ceded the Sixteen Prefectures.

fell.text: The Liao sacked Kaifeng in 947 and carried off the emperor; Liu Zhiyuan then took the throne as founder of the Later Han.

name: Later Han
summary: The shortest of the Five Dynasties, four years under the Shatuo general Liu Zhiyuan and his son.

fell.text: The general Guo Wei took Kaifeng in 951 and founded the Later Zhou.

name: Later Zhou
summary: The last of the Five Dynasties, whose emperor Shizong rebuilt the army and the treasury and began the reconquest of the south that the Song completed.

fell.text: The army proclaimed its general Zhao Kuangyin emperor at Chenqiao in 960; he founded the Song.
